design: zc-frontier-3r (zero-complexity spherical 3R: three active revolute joints whose axes meet at the glenohumeral centre GH)

frame.name: as-built frame = the model's thorax frame at the rest pose
frame.origin: GH (centre of the right glenohumeral joint)
frame.z: lateral to the right (away from the body's midline, right shoulder)
frame.model_definition: the bench's thorax frame (body_pose): x anterior, y up, z right, origin = right GH centre; the scapula frame S (J1's base) and the humerus frame H rotate about GH per pose; 'as built' = the base (scapula) held at its rest attitude, so every key pose below is given relative to the base
frame.base_attitude_note: scapula-frame direction u -> as-built RS @ u

rest_pose.definition: arm hanging at the side: plane of elevation 0, elevation 0, axial rotation 0 (elbow 90, irrelevant to the shoulder chain)

params.note: verified configuration (row docs/concepts/rows/zc-frontier-3r.json best_params; skeptic harness frozen fit60 -> 33.51)

joint_angle_definitions.theta: joint angles used here: theta = rotation of the DISTAL body relative to the PROXIMAL body, right-hand about the axis unit given (base -> link 1 about J1, link 1 -> link 2 about J2, link 2 -> member 3 about J3); theta1 = q1, theta2 = q2, theta3 = -q3 (model q below)
joint_angle_definitions.q1: J1: rotation of link 1 about the J1 axis (right-hand rule about the axis unit below), measured from the scapula's anterior direction to the J2 axis, both projected on the plane normal to J1
joint_angle_definitions.q2: J2: rotation of link 2 relative to link 1 about the J2 axis, from the J1 axis to the J3 axis (dihedral angle; 0 = folded)
joint_angle_definitions.q3: J3: rotation of member 3 (the arm) relative to link 2 about the J3 axis, from the humerus down-the-arm direction to the J2 axis
joint_angle_definitions.fk: as-built forward kinematics (base fixed): R1 = Rot(J1_rest, theta1 - theta1_rest); R2 = R1 Rot(J2_rest, theta2 - theta2_rest); R3 = R2 Rot(J3_rest, theta3 - theta3_rest); link 1 moves by R1, link 2 + hub 3 by R2, member 3 (and the upper arm) by R3; Rot = right-hand rotation about the unit axis

arcs.a1_meaning: fixed angle between the J1 and J2 axes = link 1's arc on the sphere about GH
arcs.a2_meaning: fixed angle between the J2 and J3 axes = link 2's arc
arcs.sigma_meaning: closure branch: sign of J2 . (J1 x J3) - which of the two J2 axes that satisfy both arcs the chain uses (kept for the whole motion)

J1_in_scapula_frame.rule: bvec(az, el) = (-cos el cos az, sin el, cos el sin az): az 0 posterior, 90 lateral

J3_in_humerus_frame.rule: wdir(d, a) = (sin d sin a, -cos d, sin d cos a): d from the down-the-arm axis, a 0 lateral, +90 anterior

hub_stack.type: O20 v5 hub: preloaded MR117-2RS pair (7 x 11 x 3), threaded cap
hub_stack.model_envelope: a solid disc O20 from F to F + 12.25 on the joint axis (all stack hardware and both members' plates live inside it)

J1.F_definition: distance from GH along the axis (outward) to the skin-facing face of the LOWER plate of the stack
J1.cap_side: outward (away from GH): the crown at F + 12.25

J2.F_definition: distance from GH along the axis (outward) to the skin-facing face of the LOWER plate of the stack
J2.cap_side: outward (away from GH): the crown at F + 12.25

J3.F_definition: distance from GH along the axis (outward) to the skin-facing face of the LOWER plate of the stack
J3.cap_side: outward (away from GH): the crown at F + 12.25

stack_order.meaning: inv3 = 1: at J3 link 2 is the LOWER plate (skin side, F .. F+3) and member 3 (the arm-end cap plate + neck) is on the cap side (from F + 3.15) and bridges OVER link 2 (>= 1 mm above link 2's top wherever they overlap); inv2 = 0: at J2 link 1 is the lower plate and link 2 the upper; at J1 the base is the lower plate, link 1 the upper

link1.kind: strap on the great circle between two directions from GH, underside fitted per sample (radius from GH varies)
link1.thickness_direction: radially outward from GH (underside sample r -> top r + t)
link1.model_sample_grid_order: row-major: along index (start -> end) outer, across index (offset -w/2 -> +w/2) inner

link2.kind: strap on the great circle between two directions from GH, underside fitted per sample (radius from GH varies)
link2.thickness_direction: radially outward from GH (underside sample r -> top r + t)
link2.model_sample_grid_order: row-major: along index (start -> end) outer, across index (offset -w/2 -> +w/2) inner

neck.kind: strap on the great circle between two directions from GH, underside fitted per sample (radius from GH varies)
neck.thickness_direction: radially outward from GH (underside sample r -> top r + t)
neck.model_sample_grid_order: row-major: along index (start -> end) outer, across index (offset -w/2 -> +w/2) inner

link_metal_note: the metal is a 12 x 3 strap whose UNDERSIDE follows the model's per-sample radius from GH (not a constant level); thickness 3 radially outward; its ends are held at >= the hub's F (lower member) or F + 3.15 (upper member) over the end hold, and climb <= 60 deg between samples

fold.metric: th = angle between the J1 and J3 axes (deg); a pose is allowed only if th lies in [|a1 - a2| + 5, min(a1 + a2, 360 - a1 - a2) - 5]
fold.q2_relation: cos th = cos a1 cos a2 + sin a1 sin a2 cos q2 (q2 = J2 rotation, 0 = fully folded th = |a1 - a2|, +-180 = fully stretched th = a1 + a2)
fold.hard_stops: dowel in an arc slot between link 1 and link 2 (the two bodies J2 connects), engaging at the two q2 values above

all_fit_clip_frames_kinematic.note: every frame of the 6 fit clips (held-out clips excluded), chain closure + 5 deg fold margin only, no skin check

key_poses.label: rest: arm hanging at the side, plane 0, elevation 0, axial rotation 0 (workspace-envelope pose)
across the body (largest plane of elevation among taken poses with elevation >= 40)
behind the back (Reach back pocket clip, taken frame with the largest |axial rotation|)

swept_clearances.method: base held fixed; link 2 / hub 3 rotated about J2 from rest by q2 - q2_rest over the whole fold window (121 steps); member 3 also rotated about J3 over the taken q3 span (37 steps); distance = metal sample points (underside and top faces, 2 mm grid) to the O20 hub cylinder (r 10, F .. F + 12.25) of the other joint, mm (sample spacing <= 2 mm: true distance may be up to ~1 mm less)
swept_clearances.note_fold: near the folded stop link 2 swings past hub 1: the 1 mm part-part rule (K6) holds only for q2 at or beyond the value above

bottom_interface.model_rule: K7: member 3's neck (14 wide x 6 thick Ti strap, underside fitted) runs on the great circle from the J3 axis to the direction of BOTTOM's bar start point; it is RIGID on BOTTOM (member 3 = hub-3 cap plate + neck + BOTTOM move together with the upper arm)
bottom_interface.humerus_frame: body_pose humerus frame H (rotates with the upper arm, origin GH): at rest H_x, H_y, H_z map to the as-built directions given here
bottom_interface.bar_start_point_rule: 67.5 mm out along WB + 40.0 mm down along DB from GH (H frame)
bottom_interface.neck_end_gap_note: the model's neck end sits on the bar-start DIRECTION at its own fitted underside radius, i.e. this far further out from GH than the K7 bar start point: the real part must drop from the neck end to BOTTOM's mating face (the repo's CAD does it with a bend into BOTTOM's channel)
bottom_interface.note: the model ends the neck at that direction at its fitted underside radius; the repo's L2 CAD (user style) fuses the arm-end strap into BOTTOM's channel (one 5-axis part, BOTTOM cut) or holds it by 2x / 4x M3 countersunk screws through BOTTOM's web; BOTTOM is the user's part and is not designed here

reproduction_poses: across the body (largest plane of elevation among taken poses with elevation >= 40)
behind the back (Reach back pocket clip, taken frame with the largest |axial rotation|)

provenance.protocol: fit Bench(60,160) fast (frozen) -> worn Bench(110,360) exact = the verifier protocol, 33.51
